manifest.name: @ddtcorex/dsh-maestro-govard
manifest.description: Maestro Govard bridge — thin DSH bridge for govard + workspace tools (Go stays separate)

bundle.text:
# dsh-maestro-govard bundle patch — four tool entries:
# each row loads one self-registering entry module (name/inject/apply).
- insert:
    - id: dsh-maestro-govard
      name: '@ddtcorex/dsh-maestro-govard/lib/govard-tool.js'
    - id: dsh-maestro-govard-workspace
      name: '@ddtcorex/dsh-maestro-govard/lib/workspace-tool.js'
    - id: dsh-maestro-govard-audit-lint
      name: '@ddtcorex/dsh-maestro-govard/lib/audit-lint-tool.js'
    - id: dsh-maestro-govard-deploy
      name: '@ddtcorex/dsh-maestro-govard/lib/deploy-tool.js'

readme.text:
Thin DeepSeek Harness bridge for [Govard](https://github.com/ddtcorex/govard) — exposes Govard workspace/project
tooling to DSH sessions as registered tools. The Govard engine itself is a separate Go
codebase and binary; this package only bridges, it does not embed Go code.

Part of the Maestro Harness suite (`dsh-maestro-*`). Cordis patch row id: `dsh-maestro-govard`
(short alias `maestro-govard` in the meta bundle).

- Tool registrations that shell out to the `govard` binary (environment up/down, commands in
  container, DB dumps/imports, debug configuration) with schemastery-typed parameters.
- Non-mutating deploy inspection: `govard_deploy_plan` (the resolved pipeline for a remote as its
  machine-readable `kind: "plan"` document, no connection needed) and `govard_deploy_check`
  (the preflight against a target; it leaves nothing behind there). The mutating deploy commands stay in the terminal. Both take
  `projectPath`, because the host process's own directory is rarely the project a session is
  working in — the tools fall back to the configured root, then the session workspace.
- Workspace path resolution consistent with the rest of the Maestro suite.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @ddtcorex/dsh-maestro-govard
```

The Go binary is built separately in the `govard` repository (`make build`); this bridge
expects it available on PATH or at its configured location.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm verify   # tsc --noEmit
pnpm test     # vitest run
pnpm build    # tsc -> lib/

Runtime features must be validated live against a real Govard-managed project before handoff
— see AGENTS.md.
